# F5 — The existing AURA-MAS thesis draft's literature base was AI-generated by a separate, now-inaccessible session and needs a verification pass

**Claim**: `chapter_sota.tex`, `bibliography.bib` (94 entries), and the underlying blueprint (`pasted_content_2.txt`, duplicated as `pfe_surviellance_pfe/deep-research-report.md`) were produced by a prior autonomous-agent session ("Manus AI", per `STATE_NOTES.md`) using external web search whose raw source material (the `research/*.md` sandbox files) is not present in this repository and cannot be re-verified end-to-end.

**Spot-check evidence** (this session, 6 entries checked via WebSearch): the underlying papers generally exist and are real (QMIX, MADDPG, HAWK, Murakkab, 2COOOL, RLlib, PettingZoo all verified as real works) — this rules out wholesale fabrication. However, concrete errors were found: corrupted author fields where affiliation text was merged into names ("Abbeel, OpenAI Pieter", "Moritz, Philipp reinforcement learning"), truncated author lists (single-author "et al." collapse on multi-author papers, e.g. HAWK's 4 authors reduced to "Cheng, Y."), a paraphrased/incorrect title (HAWK's bib title says "Multi-Agent Systems," actual title is "Multi-Agent Collaboration"), and at least one likely-wrong year (Murakkab bib entry says 2024 with no arXiv ID; verified arXiv ID 2508.18298 is dated August 2025).

**Confidence**: Medium (small sample, 6 of 94 entries checked; pattern is consistent enough to generalize the *recommendation* but not to certify any specific unchecked entry as correct or incorrect).

**Implication**: The existing SOTA chapter and bibliography can be used as a **starting draft / citation-discovery list**, not as submission-ready material. Every entry needs a human (or fresh, tool-verified) pass before a defense, because sloppy-but-real citations are exactly the kind of error a jury member spot-checks and that damages credibility disproportionately to the actual severity of the error.

**Related**: [[F6_existing_results_are_from_toy_scenario]] — a parallel rigor gap in the same prior-session output, on the experimental-results side rather than the literature side.
